title: Post Defense Fronting and Behind
description: A defender practises both fronting the post and playing behind with help, reading which technique the team's defense calls for.

content.objective: Deny the post entry pass using either a front or a behind-with-help technique as called.
content.setup: A post player works for position on the block against a defender.
instructions: On the 'front' call, the defender gets fully in front of the post, denying any direct pass.
On the 'behind' call, the defender plays behind with a hand in the passing lane, trusting help on a lob.
The post player works for position each rep regardless of the call.
Rotate calls randomly so the defender reacts rather than anticipates.
coachingPoints: Use the legs and a wide base to hold position when fronting.
Keep a hand up in the passing lane when playing behind.
Communicate which technique is being used to the help defense.
commonMistakes: Getting pushed under the rim when fronting without a strong base.
Fully turning the back on the ball when playing behind.
Reaching with the hands instead of moving the feet.
content.safety: Post players work for position with the body, not with elbows or grabbing.
